title: Book 7 — Polymnia, Chapter 20
paragraphs: For four full years after the conquest of Egypt he was preparing the army and the material needed for it, and in the course of the fifth year he set out on his campaign with a host of enormous size. For of all the armies of which we have any knowledge, this proved by far the greatest — so that the one Darius led against the Scythians seems nothing by comparison; nor the Scythian host, when the Scythians in pursuit of the Cimmerians invaded Media and subdued and occupied nearly the whole of upper Asia (the invasion Darius later tried to avenge); nor the force the sons of Atreus led against Ilium, to judge by the reports of their expedition; nor that of the Mysians and Teucrians, before the Trojan war, who crossed into Europe by the Bosphorus and not only subdued all the Thracians but came down as far as the Ionian Sea and marched south to the river Peneios.
